sector_model: consumer identity subscription platform (Up-C): growth, deferred revenue, FCF after SBC, tax and non-controlling interests, buybacks; not a bank or REIT model
thesis: Clear Secure (NYSE: YOU) runs the CLEAR+ identity subscription at airports and other venues. Q3 2026 (release read) revenue 292.9M (+27.8%), net income 75.3M, operating income 82.9M; 9M revenue 823.6M (+24.8%), operating income 227.9M, effective tax rate about 20%; deferred revenue 603.6M (from 516.2M at 12/31/25); FY26 FCF guide raised to at least 490M. TTM (FY2025 + 9M 2026 - 9M 2025): revenue 1,064.4M, total net income 250.6M, operating income 281.8M, OCF 491.4M, capex 33.3M, FCF about 458M, SBC 47.3M so FCF after SBC about 411M. At the 2026-11-10 close of 55.74 and 131.3M Class A plus Class C shares market cap is about 7.3B: 29x TTM total net income, 23.8x EV to operating income (net cash about 633M, debt unverified), FCF yield 6.3% (5.6% after SBC). The stock jumped 23.7% on earnings day (11-04) to a price still near the pre-release range only after that jump. Market may be pricing it as a maturing subscription business despite the growth and rising buybacks (170.9M in Q3).
counterthesis: TTM FCF is flattered by deferred revenue growth (members prepay) and still includes the Q3 outflow of about 315M for accrued partnership liabilities; the nature and whether it recurs are unread. Ownership is Up-C: non-controlling interests take about 29% of net income, so per Class A share earnings are lower than total net income (Q3 diluted Class A EPS 0.52). Cash is only 633M against 1.13B liabilities and a thin 130M equity because of buybacks and distributions; dividends, a special dividend and net-settled tax payments (51.9M) also leave cash. Airport concentration is limited (no airport over 10% of membership revenue) but the model depends on airport access and TSA relationships; competition from TSA PreCheck, Mobile ID and airline or government digital identity could limit pricing. A 23.7% one day move shows high sentiment sensitivity; 29x earnings is not cheap on GAAP.
invalidation: Net member adds or retention weakening (Q4 bookings below the 335M-340M guide), FY26 FCF below 490M, deferred revenue growth stalling, operating margin falling below about 25%, renewed negative OCF without a one-time explanation, loss of a major airport or TSA program change, or debt appearing in the unread notes that changes net cash.
